title: Spending too much on Claude
description: You can spend on Claude a bit too much #ai #claude #surfshark
transcript: When I thought we couldn't go lower, we went lower. So, no joke, someone supposedly spent 500 million US dollars worth of AI tokens on Claude, and let's take a moment of silence as this person is probably looking for a new job as we speak. But, my question is, can you blame them? Because many companies today have ridiculous requirements of forcing their employees to use AI tokens or requests. Literally, you might have KPIs to use a certain number of AI tokens per quarter, all to promote AI usage. Of course, not every job benefits from heavy use of AI, which in turn means that employees tend to ask AI stuff like, "How to take a shower? What is 2 + 2? Should I quit my job?" Well, hopefully not. But, listen, this story, I mean, I really want to believe that it's true. But, I got to be honest, I don't know if it is. For one, it's hard to find the name of the company where supposedly this happened. Some say it was Amazon, others say it was Uber. But, that aside, just how sustainable is AI use in workplaces if AI is slowly becoming more expensive and more expensive than hiring actual people who might do that same job, but for cheaper?
